style.name: Teaching Courseware - PHY4605 capstone presentation briefing
style.visual_direction: Open white or light-neutral canvas with large navy sans-serif title hierarchy, cool-gray structure, restrained blue, teal, sage, ochre and occasional coral accents, clear labelled diagrams and matrices, generous spacing, and varied layouts by slide role.
style.color_palette: white/light neutral, navy, cool gray, muted blue, teal, sage green, muted ochre, coral only for genuine warnings or defects
style.typography: large bold readable sans-serif titles, regular sans-serif body text, short labels, no decorative script, no code typography unless explicitly needed
style.texture_and_finish: flat polished teaching visual with clean cards, simple icons, evidence matrices and restrained scientific illustration
style.deck_consistency: match the approved slide 08 sample's palette, typography mood, open canvas, spacing and moderate density; vary composition by slide role; no slide numbers, outer frame, logo, watermark or timing labels

approved_style_reference.role: approved Deck B sample style reference
approved_style_reference.fidelity: match palette, title hierarchy, open canvas, icon language, density and teaching mood only; do not copy the exact four-column validation matrix

deck_context.source_summary: The presentation and defence briefing is taught in Week 07 or Week 08 so groups can use it as a working target during Weeks 09-12. The final capstone requires a defensible physical model, traceable numerical implementation, evidence-led interpretation, validation, honest limitations, transparent AI decisions, reproducible handoff and individual understanding.
deck_context.core_claim: A credible capstone is an evidence-led physical argument that can be reproduced, explained and defended—not merely a running simulation or a polished plot.
deck_context.assessment_boundary: Week 13 begins the actual presentation sequence and Week 14 continues presentations, defences and handoffs. The deck is taught earlier; it does not introduce a new Week 13 briefing chapter. Do not prescribe one graph, method, parameter change, algorithm or universal validation pair.
deck_context.platform_boundary: Submit through Google Classroom, which is the course system of record. MATLAB is the computational environment. AI assistance must be declared with concise decisions and independent checks; full chat histories are not required.
deck_context.universal_constraints: Keep visible text in English. Do not invent numerical results, equations, data, confidential exam content or a common solution route. Preserve the distinction between model output and supplied or measured data.

slides.title: Present, Defend and Hand Off Your Investigation
slides.intent: Open with the end point: an evidence-led presentation, individual defence and reproducible handoff.
key_points: Final simulation and physical interpretation
Individual defence of a model and code choice
A handoff another person can reproduce

layout.composition: open cover with presentation, defence and handoff nodes connected by an evidence ribbon

visual_elements.main_visual: three labelled end-point stations with a scientific model at the centre

slides.title: What the Final Assessment Rewards
slides.intent: Shift attention from code volume to model reasoning and accountable evidence.
key_points: Physical relevance and defensible model reasoning
Traceable numerical implementation
Evidence, validation and critical analysis
Reproducibility and individual understanding
Complexity alone is not rewarded

layout.composition: balanced evidence wheel with complexity shown outside the scoring centre

visual_elements.main_visual: six evidence lenses around a central physical claim
visual_elements.supporting_elements: ochre caution tag for complexity alone

slides.title: Turn the Scenario into a Defensible Claim
slides.intent: Teach the opening logic of a strong presentation without prescribing content.
key_points: State the real-world objective
Name the selected model and approximation
State what the evidence can support
Set the boundary of the claim

layout.composition: scenario-to-claim funnel with a clearly bounded conclusion zone

visual_elements.main_visual: scenario, model and evidence narrowing into a claim boundary
visual_elements.supporting_elements: can establish versus cannot establish labels

slides.title: Show the Model You Chose and Why
slides.intent: Make the physical model auditable and the scope choice defensible.
key_points: Show included and omitted physics
State assumptions and parameter sources
Identify initial or boundary conditions
Explain why the scope is appropriate

layout.composition: model diagram with included effects inside a boundary and omitted effects outside with reasons

visual_elements.main_visual: labelled system boundary with included and omitted effect callouts

slides.title: Explain the Realism Trade-Off
slides.intent: Connect the lecture-level baseline to a chosen realistic extension and its trade-offs.
key_points: Compare the baseline with the realistic extension
Explain the physical improvement
Identify data, computation or interpretation costs
State what remains omitted

layout.composition: layered model comparison with a trade-off balance below

visual_elements.main_visual: baseline-to-extension layers with evidence and cost arrows

slides.title: Make the Numerical Implementation Traceable
slides.intent: Show enough algorithm and implementation detail for a listener to follow the computation.
key_points: Explain the algorithm or solver choice
Show discretisation and numerical settings
Map physical terms to code structure
Name implementation decisions that affect results

layout.composition: physical equation or model block mapped through algorithm steps into annotated code structure

constraints: Do not invent code identifiers or equations
Keep code snippets generic unless supplied by the group

slides.title: Choose Evidence That Answers the Objective
slides.intent: Help students select outputs that directly support the question rather than decorate the talk.
key_points: Choose graphs, tables, animations or other evidence that answer the objective
Label units, cases, scales and assumptions
Separate model output from measured or supplied data
Explain what the audience should conclude

layout.composition: objective card linked to three evidence formats with a label-quality checklist

visual_elements.supporting_elements: units, case labels and data provenance markers

slides.title: Validate the Physics and the Computation
slides.intent: Match each test to the model claim without presenting one universal recipe.
key_points: Units test dimensional consistency
Limiting or reference behaviour tests expected physics
Convergence or sensitivity tests numerical choices
Physical plausibility and data comparison test interpretation
A running simulation is not automatically credible

layout.composition: approved representative validation matrix from model claim to four evidence lenses

visual_elements.main_visual: approved sample slide itself as style anchor; retain a four-lens matrix for this final slide

slides.title: Show Sensitivity and Uncertainty Honestly
slides.intent: Distinguish what changes the conclusion and what merely changes the presentation.
key_points: Identify parameters or settings that affect the conclusion
Separate parameter uncertainty from numerical sensitivity
State data limitations and model-form limitations
Explain whether the main claim is robust

layout.composition: robustness map with four sources of variation leading to conclusion strength

visual_elements.main_visual: sensitivity dial or tornado-style conceptual map without invented values
visual_elements.supporting_elements: parameter, numerical, data and model-form lanes

constraints: Do not invent uncertainty percentages or a required analysis method

slides.title: Explain What the Simulation Cannot Establish
slides.intent: Turn limitations into honest boundaries on the conclusion.
key_points: Link omissions to unreliable regimes
Identify data gaps and resolution limits
Separate numerical failure from model limitation
Reduce the strength of the conclusion when evidence is weak

layout.composition: claim boundary diagram with limitation gates between simulation and conclusion

visual_elements.main_visual: simulation result passing through data, resolution and model gates
visual_elements.supporting_elements: can support versus cannot establish contrast

slides.title: Record AI Decisions Transparently
slides.intent: Define concise evidence of AI use without requiring full chat histories.
key_points: Declare ChatGPT, MATLAB Copilot or other tools used
Record accepted, modified or rejected assistance
Give the reason for the decision
List independent checks performed

layout.composition: four-column decision record from request to judgement to check

visual_elements.main_visual: AI decision log cards with accepted, modified and rejected states

slides.title: Prepare a Reproducible Handoff
slides.intent: Make it possible for another person to rerun and understand the work.
key_points: Include code, data and parameter sources
Record units, MATLAB release or environment and run order
State numerical settings, tests and output instructions
List known limitations and expected evidence

layout.composition: handoff bundle opened into code, data, settings, tests and limitations

slides.title: Use an Evidence-Led Presentation Structure
slides.intent: Offer a flexible speaking sequence that keeps the physical claim central.
key_points: Objective and scenario
Model and realism decision
Algorithm and implementation
Evidence and validation
Interpretation, limitation and conclusion

layout.composition: five-stage presentation path with evidence and interpretation as the visual centre

visual_elements.main_visual: presentation flow from question to conclusion
visual_elements.supporting_elements: transition arrows and audience takeaway markers

slides.title: Prepare for the Individual Defence
slides.intent: Make the individual evidence concrete and linked to each member's understanding.
key_points: Explain one model or code choice
Trace one numerical reasoning step
Defend one validation or sensitivity check
Answer a parameter, limitation or realism follow-up

layout.composition: four defence prompt cards around an individual student and group model

visual_elements.main_visual: student defence conversation with model trace, test and follow-up prompts

slides.title: Final Lock and Submission Checklist
slides.intent: Close with a concise readiness test and the official submission route.
key_points: Model and evidence are documented
Tests and sensitivity are recorded
AI decision record is present
Clean rerun succeeds and handoff is usable
Every member is ready; submit through Google Classroom
